policy.en: Qiyas draws. The engineer and the company check and approve. Every output says For review. A value below is either a code requirement with its source (code, clause and URL) or a practice default that is labelled as one and that the engineer edits. No clause number or value here was made up: where a source could not be read, the value is a practice default.
policy.ar: قياس يرسم. المهندس والشركة يراجعان ويعتمدان. كل مخرَج مكتوب عليه: للمراجعة. كل قيمة هنا إما اشتراط كود له مصدره (الكود والبند والرابط) وإما قيمة ممارسة معتادة مكتوب أنها كذلك ويعدّلها المهندس. لم يُختلق أي رقم بند أو قيمة: حيث لم يمكن قراءة المصدر تكون القيمة ممارسة معتادة.

codes.title_en: Unified Building Law No. 119 of 2008 and its executive regulations (Ministerial Decree No. 144 of 2009)
codes.title_ar: قانون البناء الموحد رقم 119 لسنة 2008 ولائحته التنفيذية (قرار وزير الإسكان رقم 144 لسنة 2009)
codes.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities
codes.evidence_note: English translation by a law firm, read in full for the articles used below. Article numbers follow that translation; check them against the Arabic official text.
codes.use: Room sizes, ceiling height, openings, doors, stairs, railings (limits below).

codes.title_en: Egyptian Code of Practice 201: loads and forces on structures and buildings
codes.title_ar: الكود المصري 201: الأحمال والقوى على المنشآت والمباني
codes.publisher: Housing and Building National Research Center (HBRC)
codes.evidence_note: The pairing of the number and the subject was found in search results (an engineers' forum and an HBRC codes page). The edition and the exact title are not verified.
codes.use: Loads. The structural engineer applies it; Qiyas does not calculate loads.

codes.title_en: Egyptian Code of Practice 202: soil mechanics and foundations
codes.publisher: Housing and Building National Research Center (HBRC)
codes.evidence_note: Title seen in a search result for Ministerial Resolution 139 of 2001 (Egyptian code for soil mechanics and foundations). The number 202 and the edition are not verified.
codes.use: Foundations. The geotechnical and structural engineer apply it; foundation levels on a sheet are indicative.

codes.title_en: Egyptian Code of Practice 203: design and construction of reinforced concrete structures
codes.title_ar: الكود المصري 203: تصميم وتنفيذ المنشآت الخرسانية
codes.publisher: Housing and Building National Research Center (HBRC)
codes.evidence_note: Pairing of number and subject seen in a forum thread in search results; the edition is not verified.
codes.use: Reinforced concrete design. The structural engineer applies it.

codes.title_en: Egyptian Code of Practice 205: steel structures and bridges
codes.publisher: Housing and Building National Research Center (HBRC)
codes.evidence_note: An HBRC codes page seen in search results cites Code No. 205 of 2001 for metal structures and bridges. The edition in force is not verified.
codes.use: Steel structures. The structural engineer applies it.

codes.evidence_note: The SASO list of accepted inspection bodies (updated 6 September 2026) names the code and its number. The text of the code was not read.
codes.use: Architectural requirements (means of egress, stairs, doors, room heights). Values were not read: see the limits.

codes.title_en: The Saudi Residential Building Code SBC 1101 and SBC 1102
codes.title_ar: كود البناء السكني السعودي SBC 1101 و SBC 1102
codes.evidence_note: Named in the SASO list. The text was not read. Villas and houses fall under the residential code: the engineer checks room sizes and stairs against it.
Named in the SASO list. Loads are the structural engineer's.

codes.title_en: Saudi Construction Code SBC 302, Soils and Foundation Code SBC 303, Concrete Structures Code SBC 304
codes.title_ar: كود الإنشاءات SBC 302 وكود التربة والأساسات SBC 303 وكود المنشآت الخرسانية SBC 304
codes.use: Structure, foundations and concrete. The structural engineer applies them.

codes.title_en: Saudi Electrical Code SBC 401, Mechanical Code SBC 501, Sanitary Code SBC 701 (and Private Sewage Disposal SBC 702)
codes.title_ar: الكود الكهربائي SBC 401 والميكانيكي SBC 501 والصحي SBC 701 (وصرف الصرف الخاص SBC 702)
codes.use: MEP layouts on the sheets are indicative; the discipline engineer sizes and approves.

codes.evidence_note: The decree defines the code and says it is published on the Dubai Municipality website. The text of the code (Part B, villas) was not read: no value from it is used below.

codes.title_en: Abu Dhabi building codes (based on the 2009 International Codes)
codes.title_ar: أكواد البناء في أبوظبي (مبنية على الأكواد الدولية 2009)
codes.publisher: Abu Dhabi Department of Municipalities and Transport
codes.evidence_note: The ICC page says Abu Dhabi's building codes are based on the 2009 I-Codes and links the department. The current edition is not verified.

codes.title_en: UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice
codes.title_ar: كود الإمارات للحماية من الحريق وسلامة الأرواح
codes.evidence_note: The ICC page links the national fire code PDF. The PDF could not be opened from here: no value from it is used below.

limits.note: Clear height from finished floor to the underside of the exposed ceiling, every floor.
Entrances, internal corridors, bathrooms, laundry rooms, guards' rooms and similar spaces.
Openings for light and ventilation: 8% of the floor area of residential rooms. Living, dining and reception count as residential rooms.
10% of the floor area of a bathroom, kitchen, toilet or stairwell. Distribution halls, corridors and entrances are exempt.
A door that opens directly onto a stair flight must be at least one metre from it.
Window sill, unless a balcony, terrace or a railing of at least 0.9 m is in front of it.
Clear length of the step, floors with up to four units (a villa has one). 1.30 m for the main stair when a floor has more than four units.
At most 14 consecutive steps, then a landing at least four treads wide.
Stair railing 0.90 m. Terrace and balcony railings 0.90 m for the first five floors, plus 5 cm for each floor after, up to 1.20 m; it must stop objects of 10 cm or more falling.

limits.rationale: Common clear height for habitable rooms in Egyptian and Gulf housing. Not read from the KSA or UAE code text. The engineer confirms it against the code that applies.
Common lower height for corridors, bathrooms and service rooms. Not read from the code text.
A bedroom or living room under about 9 square metres is hard to furnish. Practice, not a code value.
A bed and a passage beside it need about this width. Practice, not a code value.
A kitchen with units on two walls and a passage. Practice, not a code value.
Units on one side plus a working passage. Practice, not a code value.
WC, basin and shower or bath with clearances. Practice, not a code value.
Practice, not a code value.
A guest WC with a basin. Practice, not a code value.
Practice, not a code value.
A clear passage inside a house. No corridor width was read in the Egyptian regulations or the other codes. Practice, not a code value.
Common clear leaf for a room door. The Egyptian regulations give the same figure (Article 97); KSA and UAE text was not read.
Kitchens, bathrooms and toilets. Practice, not read from the KSA or UAE text.
A villa main entrance is a wide single leaf (1.20 m) or a double leaf (1.50 m and more). No code value was read; it is the way villas are designed in the region.
Space to stop before a stair. The Egyptian regulations give one metre (Article 96); KSA and UAE text was not read.
Common rule of thumb for daylight. Not read from the KSA or UAE text.
Practice, not a code value.
Above 0.9 m, or protected by a railing. Practice, not read from the code text.
Clear width of a private stair in a house. The Egyptian regulations ask 1.10 m (Article 100). KSA and UAE text was not read.
Comfortable tread for a private stair. Practice, not read from the KSA or UAE text.
Comfortable riser for a private stair. Practice, not read from the KSA or UAE text.
A landing after this many steps keeps a fall short. Practice, not a code value.
Clear height above every step. The Egyptian regulations give 2.10 m (Article 100).
Stair, balcony and terrace railings. The Egyptian regulations give 0.90 m (Articles 100 and 103); KSA and UAE text was not read, so the safer figure is used.
